clue.text: Former longings out of time — collections of odds and ends to suffice here

definitions.text: collections of odds and ends to suffice here

parts.note: former times are the past

indicators.note: out of time says the time letter is dropped from the longings word

parts.note: itches are cravings or longings

explanation.surface: Someone nostalgic for old desires that have run out of time, gathering scraps that will do for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes T from ITCHES, leaving ICHES.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a medley assembled from borrowed fragments, a hotchpotch put together to serve.

clue.text: Great rocks appearing after work turning over kitchen garden

indicators.note: the rocked letters come after the turned work word
turning over in a down clue flips the work word so it reads upwards

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: rocks means shakes up, so the letters of great are jumbled

explanation.surface: Huge boulders turning up after digging in a vegetable plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' makes PO from OP; 'rocks' turns GREAT into TAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Potager is the French-derived word for an ornamental vegetable garden by the kitchen.

clue.text: Holy man dealing with the heavens, not good regarding columns

parts.note: ST, saint, is a holy man

indicators.note: not good says the good letter is removed

parts.note: galactic describes matters of the galaxy and the heavens

explanation.surface: A saint who deals with heavenly matters but is no good at architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops G from GALACTIC, leaving ALACTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalactic is the adjective for stalactites, the hanging columns of cave rock.

clue.text: Ultimately accepting it on the largest scale

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the Latin phrase holds the word it

parts.note: in fine is Latin for finally or in the end

explanation.surface: In the end, embracing something on a grand scale.
explanation.walkthrough: IN FINE is a Latin phrase meaning at last, still found in older English; 'accepting' puts IT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something boundless or limitless is on a scale beyond any larger one.

clue.text: Point of control initially installed in home, mostly inexplicable stuff

indicators.note: installed in means placed inside the shortened home word
mostly means all but the final letter of the home word

parts.note: a house is a home
a cusp is a pointed end or point

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letters of the words of and control

explanation.surface: A control point fitted in a home, mostly baffling gadgetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the heads of two words, 'of control', so 'of' is a fodder word, not a link; 'mostly' and 'installed in' then build the home around the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Hocus-pocus is meaningless mumbo-jumbo or trickery that baffles the onlooker.

clue.text: Son with passion to become a gentleman

parts.note: ire is anger, a strong passion

explanation.surface: A boy whose fiery temper makes him a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Sire is an old respectful title for a man of rank, a lord or king.

clue.text: Bear onset of business collapse

indicators.note: onset of takes the opening letter of business

parts.note: ruin is a collapse or downfall

explanation.surface: A bear market heralding the start of a business going under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the stock-market sense, matching the business surface; it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruin is a folk name for a bear, from the Reynard fables.

clue.text: Lads expressing love over that woman offering poetic name

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece is over, above, the next
expressing in its sense of pressing out squeezes the love letter from the lads word

parts.note: boys are lads
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
she refers to that woman

explanation.surface: Young men declaring love to a woman and coming up with a name for a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressing' means squeezing out, so O leaves BOYS, giving BYS. Percy Bysshe Shelley was the Romantic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Bysshe was the middle name of the poet Shelley, so it is a poet's name.

clue.text: Nice article about sex for couple

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the French article goes round the sex word

parts.note: une is the French indefinite article, as used in Nice
it is a crossword stand-in for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A pleasant piece about sex aimed at a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective, hence a French article.
explanation.definitionFit: To couple things is to join or link them together, a verb synonym.

clue.text: One old soldier put in negative vote, displaying simple response

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the vote word

parts.note: nay is a vote against
I is the Roman numeral one
VET, veteran, is an old soldier

explanation.surface: A veteran casting a no vote, showing an unsophisticated reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocent, unsophisticated simplicity in how someone reacts.

clue.text: One loudly boarding vehicle turned to see all the other vehicles

indicators.note: boarding means getting into, so these letters go inside the turned vehicle
turned says the vehicle word is read backwards

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle
FF, fortissimo, is very loudly in music
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A noisy passenger getting on a vehicle that has turned to look at the rest of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes TRAC from CART; 'boarding' puts FFI inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic is the mass of vehicles on the road besides one's own.

clue.text: Italian composer angry after contralto decamps in Italy

indicators.note: decamps means leaves, so the contralto letter departs from the angry word

parts.note: cross means angry
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A cross Italian composer once his contralto walks out mid-tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decamps' drops C from CROSS, leaving ROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini wrote The Barber of Seville, a famous Italian opera composer.

clue.text: Returned to finish tucking into some wine, expressing joy

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside the wine word

parts.note: a glass is some wine

indicators.note: returned says the finish word is read backwards

parts.note: end means finish

explanation.surface: Coming back to polish off some wine, showing delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' turns the finish word round, and 'tucking into' sends it into the measure of wine; 'expressing' is just a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladness is happiness and delight, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Head of kitchen not fine, about to imagine backing dairy product

indicators.note: about means going round, so the shortened chef word surrounds the turned imagine word
not fine says the fine letter is removed

parts.note: a chef is the head of a kitchen
F is an abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: backing says the imagine word is read backwards

parts.note: to see something is to imagine it

explanation.surface: A chef, off form, is about to dream up a milk product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads like 'about to', meaning soon; here it is the container signal, with 'not' and 'backing' working inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese is made from curdled milk, a classic dairy food.

clue.text: Knight having staff restrained by electronic weapon is a harsh overseer

indicators.note: restrained by means held inside the weapon word

parts.note: a Taser is an electric stun weapon
K is the chess abbreviation for knight
a mast is a staff or pole

explanation.surface: A knight with a stick subdued by a stun gun is a brutal boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A taskmaster drives others hard, a strict supervisor of work.

clue.text: Going in circles on a trail to Barking

indicators.note: barking means mad, so these letters go wild

explanation.surface: A dog going round and round on the trail to the town of Barking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' looks like the London district, but it is the slang word for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotational motion is turning about an axis, going round in circles.

clue.text: Male companion with unknown inamorata

parts.note: a lad is one of the lads, a male friend
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A boyfriend with a mystery sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman who is loved, a lady love.

clue.text: Cinema area sadly missing a trace of England — Hollywood stuff, say

indicators.note: sadly says the cinema area letters are jumbled, and missing says the England letter is among them but absent from the result
a trace of takes just the first letter of England

explanation.surface: A cinema's surroundings, sadly lacking any hint of Englishness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly missing': CINEMA AREA rearranged makes the answer plus one E, the letter 'a trace of' takes from England.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana are artefacts typical of American culture, of which Hollywood products are an example.

clue.text: A wally's upset about carpet marks

indicators.note: about means going round the carpet word
upset in a down clue turns the words upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: a wally and a git are both British insults for a fool, here with the possessive s
a mat is a small carpet

explanation.surface: A fool knocked over around the rug leaves stains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the fool and the A upwards together, and 'about' makes that reversed run wrap the carpet. Wally and git are both British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Stigmata are marks on the body, especially resembling Christ's wounds.

clue.text: Forward and upward process for boats

definitions.meaning: in rugby a forward playing in the second row
a canal chamber where boats are raised by water

explanation.surface: A rugby player and a canal mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the second-row forward has this name; on canals the gated chamber raises boats.

clue.text: Network about to go down? That requires advanced course

indicators.note: about means surrounding the second word

parts.note: LAN is a local area network
to sag is to droop or go down
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: If the computer network is about to fail, that calls for an advanced class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a dish in a meal, not a course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagna is an Italian pasta dish served as a course of a meal.

clue.text: Soldiers an inspiration guarding King, terse in action

indicators.note: guarding means enclosing the king letter

parts.note: a muse is a source of inspiration
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: in action means the letters are put into motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Troops fired up protecting their king, curt in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guarding' and 'in action' both sound military, fitting the soldiers, but they are the container and anagram signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Musketeers were soldiers armed with muskets, like Dumas's famous trio.

clue.text: Church about to support venal behaviour for real

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: sin covers corrupt wrongdoing
CE is the Church of England
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: The church is about to back corruption, genuinely.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means genuine and honest, meant in earnest.

clue.text: Name entered in roll, omitting last letter

indicators.note: in means placed inside the shortened roll word
omitting last letter cuts the final letter from the roll word

parts.note: a reel is a roll, as of film or thread
to put something down is to enter it, as on a list

explanation.surface: A name written on a register, missing its final letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omitting last letter' trims the roll before 'in' places the entered word inside it; the surface suggests the name is trimmed, but it is the roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A good name is one's reputation, and repute means the same.

clue.text: Hospital employee is coming in the back, mostly

indicators.note: coming in means entering the shortened back word
mostly means all but the last letter of the back word

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A hospital worker entering by the rear door, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the back of a ship, and 'coming in' puts the word is inside. A hospital sister is a British term for a senior nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward.

clue.text: Standard component of rifle

definitions.meaning: regular, ordinary, as in a usual line of goods
the wooden butt and handle part of a gun

explanation.surface: A standard part of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock means standard, as in stock phrase; it is also the shaped wooden body of a rifle.

clue.text: Hero of group in nerve centre

indicators.note: of the group puts the hero after the group word

parts.note: a gang is a group
a lion is a celebrated hero, as in literary lion

explanation.surface: The champion of a team at the heart of operations.
explanation.definitionFit: A ganglion is a cluster of nerve cells, a centre in the nervous system.

clue.text: Satisfied with elevation, securing a group of players

indicators.note: securing means holding the letter a inside
elevation in a down clue raises the word so it reads upwards

parts.note: met as in met a demand, satisfied it

explanation.surface: Pleased with a promotion, holding onto a squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with elevation' turns MET into TEM; 'securing' puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A team is a side of players in a sport.

clue.text: Attempt to catch large blue bouncing blob

indicators.note: to catch means holding the large letter inside the attempt word

parts.note: a go is an attempt
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: bouncing means jumping about, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Trying to catch a big blue bouncy ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' puts L in GO; 'bouncing' turns BLUE into BULE.
explanation.definitionFit: A globule is a small round drop or blob of liquid.

clue.text: Important viewpoint mangled by Spooner as food item

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: key means important
a take is a point of view

explanation.surface: A crucial opinion garbled by the reverend as something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the K and T sounds of KEY TAKE gives TEA CAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a sweet bun, often toasted, eaten with tea.

clue.text: Bug taking out first joint

indicators.note: taking out first removes the opening letter of the bug word

parts.note: to bug is to irritate, and to rankle is to cause lasting irritation

explanation.surface: An insect removed from the first marijuana cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like a cannabis cigarette beside 'Bug'; it is the body joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle joins the foot to the leg, a joint of the body.

clue.text: Preserve horse, keeping a lot of illness suppressed

indicators.note: keeping means holding the cut illness word inside the horse word

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, dropping its last letter

parts.note: a malady is an illness

explanation.surface: Saving a horse while holding back most of its sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims the illness and 'keeping' puts it inside the horse; 'suppressed' only reinforces the picture of something held in.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus preserve, a jam made with oranges.
